text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Moi warns Nakuru and Kisumu residents of dire consequences if they attend unlicensed rallies calling for constitutional reform scheduled for Saturday.
- Pope's representative in Kenya condemns attacks and harassment of Roman Catholic workers in Turkana district.
- Lands Minister Ngala says government has launched programme to identify public land with view to protecting it from speculators.
- Members of Consultative Council of Islamic Party of Kenya vow to use "secret means" to return exiled preacher Sheikh Khalid Balala from Germany.
- Opposition leaders say they want to meet President Moi over call for constitutional reforms.
- Vehicle carrying 30 police recruits involved in accident with tractor along Nyeri-Nanyuki road, central province.
- President Moi asks chiefs to mobilise Kenyans to register as voters.
- Canadian High Commissioner to Kenya Bernard Dussault appeals to Kenyans calling for constitutional reforms to adopt non-violent approach.

- Tanzania's National Bank of Commerce will be split into three after 1972 Public Corporations Act is amended to give president powers to dissolve any corporation without recourse to National Assembly.

- Kenya Breweries Limited appeals to Tanzanian Treasury to ignore recommendation by government task force to increase taxes on its beer brands by 105 percent while lowering taxes on South African and Dutch brands by 38.5 percent.
